title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: September 18 | Week 1 vs. Los Angeles Chargers
headline: Jeremiyah Love will not get an expanded role despite a full week of practice; Arizona plans to rotate its backs and ride the hot hand.
summary: LaFleur downplayed the idea that a full week of practice would expand Jeremiyah Love's role. He said the backs will rotate because it is a long season and the position takes a beating, and that he has no idea how many carries Love will get. The hot hand will stay in the game, as with a basketball star who is hitting shots. He said Love is getting more comfortable as the game slows down, and he backed the rookie breaking a designed up-the-middle touchdown run outside. He praised Trey McBride for playing at his own pace because the game has slowed down for him. He said Roy has a minor groin issue and answered "we'll see" on his weekend availability. He then discussed an opposing 'chess piece' defender he fully expects to play, a nickel/linebacker hybrid, and called the opposing defense a well-coached machine. The coach also covered special teams, which he said played tremendously last Sunday, and said Arizona practiced outside partly to prepare for a hot game at San Francisco in Week 3. The transcript's content points to Seattle as the opponent even though the title says the Chargers, so the opponent is unclear.

injuries.detail: The coach said Roy has "a little bit of a groin" and added "we'll see" on whether he is a concern this weekend. The captions give only the first name, so the identification is moderately confident.

signals.claim: Love will not get an expanded role this week; the backs will rotate and the hot hand will get more work.
signals.note: Workload is unpredictable, so there is no guaranteed volume bump despite his growing comfort; touches may depend on game flow.
signals.quote: we'll keep the hot hand in there, whoever that may be.

signals.note: The coach says the game has slowed down for McBride and he plays at his own pace, which is a positive sign for his consistency.
signals.quote: He plays harder than anyone on the field every snap.

He said special teams played tremendously on Sunday with some things to clean up, and that the challenge is to repeat it. He credits the personnel staff for roster decisions that weigh special-teams value.
Arizona practiced outdoors partly to prepare for a possible 100-degree day at San Francisco in Week 3. He said Saturday walkthroughs are standard and mentally focused.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 2 Media Availability | Friday, September 18th | Press Conference

AJ Terrell and Chris (likely Lindstrom, the guard) are both questionable and will be monitored over the next 24 hours. Za'Darius Smith is handling more physically and mentally as his shoulder improves, and his role will keep growing. Divine Deablo wore the green dot for the first time in the regular season and was praised for it. Stefanski also called Panthers QB Bryce Young terrific, especially on off-schedule plays.

title: Jesse Minter Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Week 2

summary: Minter said Friday's practice went well and the team is excited for its first real home game. He said some injured players would be evaluated over roughly the next hour after practice, so their status was not settled. He expressed high confidence in the depth, pointing to the reps players have taken since OTAs and through camp. On Nnamdi Madubuike, he would only say the team has to wait and see. Travis Jones ("TJ") was the one player he called definitely out, with the possibility of more absences still open. He praised Carson Vinson as one of the most improved players; Vinson played in jumbo packages in Week 1 and is physical and aggressive. On the many Week 1 penalties, he said some are a cost of doing business at game speed, but he wants pre-snap penalties cleaned up, and he expects home-crowd noise to help the offense. He also said the Ravens worked out Brandin Cooks as part of the ongoing search for the best 70 players, after losing a player named "Jacoby" and promoting a practice-squad veteran to the roster.

title: Joe Brady Breaks Down Week 2 Victory Over Detroit Lions | Buffalo Bills
headline: DJ Moore (injury) might miss a game and Ed Oliver was a late scratch, so Keon Coleman and Skyler Bell are the WR names to watch; Dalton Kincaid's blocking is keeping him on the field.
summary: Brady said the Bills are waiting on test and MRI results for the players hurt in the Thursday night win over Detroit. They will not practice again until next Wednesday because of the long weekend, so recovery time matters. He called DJ Moore as tough as they come and said Moore will play if he can, though the injury could cost him a game. Ed Oliver was ruled out minutes before inactives were due, because the Bills wanted Mike Danna active for Detroit's heavy run volume. Keon Coleman took over Moore's plays after Moore went down, and Brady praised him and the trust Josh Allen has in him, including on a key third-down conversion. Dalton Kincaid's offseason strength work is showing in his blocking, and Brady said the tight end group, including Dawson Knox and Keleki Latu, is giving the offense real versatility in 12, 13 and 14 personnel. Deone Walker's role grew when Oliver went out and Brady said his arrow is up. Brady said Skyler Bell is handling being inactive well and will be ready when his turn comes. Brady also owned the end-of-first-half clock management and said the team's identity is still being worked out. He said Ty Johnson and T.J. Sanders were close to being cleared for Thursday.

title: Dave Canales gives final updates before Sunday's game against Falcons
headline: Jalen Coker returned to full practice, but John Metchie III was moved into a trusted-target role for Bryce Young as insurance; Pat Jones II remains questionable and day-to-day.

He praised Jones's physical, versatile pass-rush and run-game impact. Trevis Gipson was highlighted as a versatile, dependable option who can rush inside or outside and play early downs and special teams. On offense, Canales explained that John Metchie III's move was about Bryce Young trusting him and his versatility, prompted by the early-week question marks on Jalen Coker. Coker progressed to full participation on Friday. Metchie also gets punt return opportunities, though Canales said that wasn't the reason for the move. Atlanta is expected to start Cooper Rush; Canales respects him, doesn't expect to change the game plan, and noted the Falcons could use Wildcat looks. He credited Bryce Young's confidence and command of the system for his success against Atlanta, saying the call sheet feels bigger when Young is locked in. He also said the run defense's week-one problems stemmed from time of possession rather than conditioning, and that Michael Jackson will be up this week as a big run-stuffing, pocket-pushing lineman.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears’ keys to success vs. Vikings | Press Conference

He said the Bears have a good mix of designed plays for Caleb Williams, who also creates organically with his legs, and called that a luxury for the offense. Asked about spreading the ball after a 59-point Week 1, he said every active skill player (Loveland, Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, Cole Kmet, both running backs) will be a primary receiver at times, but he can't predict where the ball goes each week. He noted Kalif Raymond led the team in Week 1 and lauded his fearlessness and work ethic on punt returns. On the Vikings, he highlighted Aaron Jones, Justin Jefferson and Addison, plus the tight ends, and called Harrison Smith a major problem who was likely situational last week. He noted that Minnesota may play two quarterbacks and that the Bears will stick to their plan. title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 18th, 2026
headline: Fannin is called a weapon, but Monken blamed the 49-snap offense for his three Week 1 targets. Watson was more decisive and has taken all the first-team reps. Tyson Campbell's ankle held up in practice, though no Sunday status was given.
summary: Monken said Tyson's ankle responded to returning to practice and that he moved around well, but he would not confirm a Sunday status until after practice. A reporter asked about a backup center who has been out a while. Monken said the team will have to see whether he is even the backup center. On Week 1, he blamed the lack of stacked plays early and a total of 49 snaps for the thin target volume, and he did not promise Harold Fannin Jr. more targets, though he called him a weapon. He attributed the run game's struggles partly to Tampa-caliber opposition, partly to it being the first game, and partly to a new staff and an offensive line still gelling with the tight ends. He expects the run game to grow. He praised Deshaun Watson as more decisive, especially throwing downfield, after taking all the first-team reps in the week leading up to the game. He said Tampa Bay's defense stresses run and protection rules with pressure from every edge and secondary pressures. He described Bucky Irving as explosive with excellent contact balance, and said Mike Evans-type receivers (Godwin and the others) are players any quarterback can trust. The team is also trying to fix pre-snap and substitution issues by shortening the practice clock and running subs from the sideline.

title: Brian Schottenheimer on 105.3 The Fan | 9-18-26

He cited good halftime adjustments on offense and good plays from Caleb Downs, and he said the Cowboys forced several fumbles that didn't bounce their way. He downplayed the viral sideline exchange between defensive coordinator Christian Parker and Jaishawn Barham as frustration from a young, talented player. title: HC Sean Payton on the Broncos’ home-field advantage: ’We feed off that’
headline: Payton says Jaylen Waddle will get his touches after the team's intent to involve him early went unmet in Week 1; practice focus was third down and red zone ahead of a short-week home game.
summary: Payton described the week as one of good energy and focus, with both practices feeling sharp after a tough loss on Monday night. He said the team has been honest about corrections, noting the kicking game went well, and that the loss was addressed directly with the players. Preparation has centered on third down, with red zone work planned for Saturday that will be more extensive than a typical Saturday practice. He praised the opposing quarterback (Lawrence) as a big-armed, mobile passer who can punish a defense that rushes poorly in man coverage, and said the supporting cast looks confident and experienced together. Payton stressed that home-field advantage is significant because crowd noise, silent counts and motions are much harder to deal with on the road, and said the Broncos feed off their crowd. On offense, he said the team's intent in Week 1 was to get Jaylen Waddle involved, and they need to be more deliberate without forcing it, but Waddle will get his touches. He also discussed 13 personnel and heavier groupings, saying they close the edges, reduce the defense's menu and help the tackles, and that balance between run and play-action remains the commitment on early downs. On the return game, he said several players have been repped at returner depending on where punts come from, without naming a clear replacement.

signals.note: Payton acknowledged the plan to get Waddle involved early fell short and pledged a more deliberate approach, which raises his target outlook.

On the league trend toward 13 personnel, Payton said heavier sets close the edges and shrink the defensive menu, helping tackles, but a team still must stay balanced with the run game and play action.
With a returner injured, Payton said several players have been repped at the position, with the choice depending on punt location, and he gave no firm answer.
The short week after Monday night makes recovery important, and the new facility saves time because everything is close for players.

title: Campbell on Week 2 performance
headline: Lions' run game is the top concern after a Week 2 loss at Buffalo; Campbell vows to fix it, and Avonte Maddox's injury (left on crutches) could hurt the secondary ahead of the Jets.
summary: Campbell took responsibility for a poor Week 2 loss to the Bills, saying the Lions were out-played and out-coached in all three phases and fell behind by three scores after stalling early. He said the run game must be far more efficient and consistent, calling it the key to the offense, and said there is a lot of room to grow. He blamed the early struggles on a new-look Bills defense that used more safety pressures and ran the Lions down from the backside, which forced Detroit to throw. Defensively, he pointed to explosive plays, busts in the back end, wrong gap fits, and failing to contain the mobile Bills quarterback, who also converted many third-and-shorts. He attributed the secondary's problems to communication and playing together, and said he stands by the aggressive approach. He expressed confidence in the defensive front, saying it has pass rush and run-stopping ability. Avonte Maddox was seen on crutches and did not return; Campbell said that makes him nervous and he will know more tomorrow. The team now turns to the Jets after a short window to review two games of tape.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Rookie Anthony Hill starts at Mike for Tennessee, and Cedric Gray is expected to clear protocol, which could mean a linebacker rotation with Cody Barton.
summary: Saleh began with injuries. Cordale Flott popped up with tightness after practice and will not practice Friday, but Saleh has no concern about him for the game. Saleh confirmed Anthony Hill is starting at Mike, and he praised the young linebacker, saying the hardest part for a young Mike is communication and that Hill has Barton, Amani Hooker, Kevin Winston and an experienced D-line to help. He also liked Oluwafemi Oladejo's first game as an edge rusher: strong against the run, clean overall, still raw as a pass rusher, and close to a sack on one play.
